description: New York DL, layout taken from an issued credential. PII replaced.

provenance.source: PDF417 barcode decoded from an issued New York driver's license (AAMVA v10, IIN 636001)
provenance.anonymization: Every identifying value was replaced with a placeholder of the same byte length and character class, so the encoded layout is byte-for-byte unchanged: DCS/DAC/DAD (names), DAQ (customer ID), DAG/DAI/DAK (address, NY ZIP prefix kept), DCF, DBB/DBD/DBA (dates, shifted), and both ZN elements — ZNA keeps the card's LAST@FIRST@MIDDLE shape and ZNB is filled to its observed 90 characters. DDB (card revision date) describes the card stock rather than the holder and is unchanged, as are DCA/DCB/DCD/DBC/DAY/DAU/DDA/DDD and the DDE/DDF/DDG truncation flags.
provenance.notes: Reproduces the source card's directory exactly: DL at offset 41 declaring 323 bytes, ZN at 364 declaring 120, 484 bytes total, jurisdiction version 04. Getting there took three things the card had to be measured for, all now in NY's encoding profile: 100 bytes of space fill across ten elements at widths that are mostly New York's own rather than AAMVA's (names to 25 where the spec allows 40, vehicle class to 4 where it allows 6); the final element of each subfile closed by the segment terminator alone, with no separator before it, which is where the last byte of each subfile went; and the jurisdiction version. The element order needed nothing — it already matched the schema default.
